rv.q: It's a rare actor who can make two hours of theological introspection entertaining, but Suchet is that actor.
But it’s Tom Littler’s hugely inventive production that really draws us into this version, staged at St John the Divine, across the road from the Orange Tree in Richmond , west London.
I can pretty much guarantee that you won't see anything as strange, challenging and fascinating on a London stage this year.

Always a meticulous actor, Suchet makes each gesture and syllable precise and shows the making up of Becket’s mind in the responsive phase and then brings the clarity and verbal relish of the best Shakespearean soliloquies to the Christmas Day sermon in which the turbulent priest accepts that he must be killed.
Eliot was not much of a playwright and this is more arcane, tortured hagiography than it is tragedy.
But this performance, directed by the Orange Tree Theatre's Tom Littler with associate director Francesca Ellis, and starring David Suchet is an absolute triumph.
Littler's Murder in the Cathedral takes an already beautiful text and then knocks it out of the park in all aspects of the production.

cn.t: Critics praise this audacious staging of T.S. Eliot's verse drama, with David Suchet delivering gravitas in the lead role. The atmospheric church setting and excellent production do justice to Eliot's beautiful verse about Thomas Becket's martyrdom.
